Let's get started with today's live broadcast. ## Scene Setup ### Initial Steps - First, we will sew up the board. - After sewing, we choose this board and harden it, placing it in front of our chest. ### Chest Pad Attachment - The next step is crucial: we need to ensure that the chest pad can be attached to the model. - To achieve this, I added negative pressure to it. - After applying negative pressure, we adjust the shape of the chest pad. ### Surface Adjustment - Next, we adjust the surface of the virtual model to zero, then select the board. - You can reduce its particle diameter first, followed by reducing the conflict thickness. ### Hardening and Material Application - You will see that we can remove the hardening, then adjust the shape of the chest pad. - Now, let's add a material to the chest pad and draw the inner line on it. - After drawing the inner line, we select it and engrave an outer layer for it, creating a double-layer thickness. ## Simulation Process ### Positioning and Adjustment - Let's simulate the model. Due to the negative pressure of the board, it can be tightly attached to the model. - We can use the positioning ball tool to adjust its position and open the simulation again. ### Final Adjustments - Adjust the chest pad shape a few more times slowly. - When the shape is almost adjusted, we can use the positioning ball tool to secure it to prevent movement. ### Chest Shape Adjustment - To adjust the thickness of the fabric, we can change the thickness of the chest, making it more full. ## Sewing the Plates ### Plate Alignment - Next, we will remove the joint of one of the plates and align it with the other two plates. - We can adjust the position of the chest by aligning it with both sides of the chest. ### Simulation - After turning on the simulation, you will see that the chest is firmly attached to the model. - Rotate to check the shape of the chest. ### Freezing the Chest - Once the chest is finished, we can freeze it to prevent changes while working on other positions. ## Creating the Chest ### Plate Selection - We start by selecting all the plates and making a selection. - Next, we open the front plate, enlarging the screen for better visibility. ### Copying Plates - Select the top two plates and copy them, applying the same to the back plate. - We will twist it aside temporarily. ### Negative Pressure Adjustment - After selecting the plates, we can pull down on the right side of the calculator to find the negative pressure option and change it to negative. ## Arranging and Sewing Plates ### Plate Arrangement - We can now arrange the plates by moving all the front plates to one side. - Select the front plate and arrange it accordingly. ### Sewing Process - Enter the sewing machine to quickly sew our plates together. - Sew the side seams according to the alignment points. ## Material Adjustments ### Zipper Application - Finally, we add a zipper on the back to avoid hitting the back plate, adjusting its width as necessary. ### Simulation and Shape Adjustment - Start the simulation and adjust the shape of the clothes, ensuring the bottom part is flat. - Address the front chest position, as the plate is stretched and may open too wide. ## Elasticity Adjustment ### 100% Elasticity Setting - To prevent the clothing from being pulled apart, select the edges and add 100% elasticity. - After setting the elasticity, start the simulation to see the effects. ### Final Adjustments - Continue simulating and adjusting the shape of the clothing as necessary, ensuring it fits the model properly. ## Creating the Bandage ### Bandage Design - We will design the bandage on the back, starting by selecting the holes on the bandage with the Blur tool. - Transform these holes into an internal pattern. ### Adjustment and Selection - Use the adjustment panel tool to select the closed space of the internal pattern and transform it into a hole. ### Creating Tape Position - To create a border preventing the fabric from sticking together, we will use a column layer for the inner circle of the panel and cut it accordingly. ## Stitching and Simulation ### Stitching the Bandage - Use the sewing tool to stitch the decorative bandage effect. - Adjust the fabric properties to ensure they align correctly. ### Simulation and Final Touches - After finishing the bandage, we can simulate the entire design. - Make necessary adjustments, ensuring the design flows well. ## Adding Decorative Elements ### Creating Flowers - To create flowers, observe the shape of the petals and draw them out using the board tool. - Adjust the particle diameter for finer details, and apply a fabric material. ### Flower Assembly - Assemble the petals by linking them and sewing them together. - Simulate to see how they interact with the model. ## Final Adjustments and Simulation ### Rendering and Effects - After completing the design, we can render the final output. - Adjust transparency and materials for visual effects. ### Animation and Exporting - Switch to animation mode and save the work as needed. - Adjust settings and export the final animation for presentation. ## Conclusion This concludes our session on the 3D modeling and scene setup for swimwear production. If you have any questions, feel free to ask. Thank you for joining the live broadcast!
